description: Buckeye State Bank (Powell, Ohio) SBA loan rates: 7(a) caps from 10.00% with prime at 7.00%, how this Ohio community bank lends, and questions to ask.
lede: Buckeye State Bank is an Ohio community bank based in Powell, north of Columbus, that makes SBA-guaranteed loans alongside its conventional business lending.
about: Buckeye State Bank is a state-chartered community bank headquartered in Powell, Ohio, in the northern suburbs of Columbus. It began in 1885 as The Citizens Bank of De Graff, a small-town bank in Logan County, and moved its main office to Powell in 2018 as it shifted its focus toward the Columbus market. The bank still keeps offices in west-central Ohio where it started.

The bank grew south when it acquired Rockhold Bank, a community bank in Ross County, adding offices around Bainbridge and the Chillicothe area. The result is a small branch network that spans growing Columbus suburbs and rural southern Ohio towns. Decisions are made locally, which matters for borrowers whose loan does not fit a national bank's scorecard.

Its business clients are mostly owner-operated companies: contractors, professional practices, service firms, retailers and family businesses buying property or equipment. The bank participates in the SBA 7(a) program and uses it for deals that need a longer term or lower down payment than a conventional loan allows. Expect a relationship approach, with deposit accounts and treasury services usually part of the package.
sba_fit: A borrower in central Ohio would most often bring Buckeye State Bank a 7(a) loan for buying an existing business, purchasing an owner-occupied building or refinancing expensive equipment debt. Because it is a smaller bank, an SBA guarantee lets it take on loans larger or riskier than it would hold alone. Ask whether it has Preferred Lender status, since that affects how fast approval comes. For a larger building project, ask whether it will act as the first-lien lender on a 504 loan with a Columbus-area CDC.
known_for: Community bank headquartered in Powell, north of Columbus

faqs.a: Yes. Buckeye State Bank appears in SBA lending data as a participating 7(a) lender. Call its business lending team to confirm which SBA programs it offers today, the loan sizes it prefers, and whether it can approve loans in-house under SBA's Preferred Lender Program.

faqs.q: Where is Buckeye State Bank located?
faqs.a: Its headquarters is in Powell, Ohio, a suburb north of Columbus. The bank started in De Graff in Logan County and also has offices in southern Ohio from its acquisition of Rockhold Bank, including the Bainbridge area of Ross County.

faqs.q: What rate will I pay on a Buckeye State Bank SBA loan?
faqs.a: The bank sets your rate, but it cannot exceed SBA caps. With prime at 7.00%, variable 7(a) caps range from 10.00% for loans over $350,000 to 13.50% for loans of $50,000 or less. Your actual rate depends on size, term, collateral and cash flow.
